Input granularity: single element — one sequence per analysis, from an accession, a file or pasted text; a whole assembly is read only by the primer off-target scan (app/backend/engine.py)
De novo structural detection: yes — terminal repeat, terminal inverted repeat and target-site duplication detectors with published thresholds (app/backend/teagle_core/structural.py)
Protein-domain classification: yes — bundled 30-model Pfam-A panel searched with HMMER via pyhmmer (app/backend/teagle_core/domains.py)
Homology-based family naming: partial — optional Dfam naming through RepeatMasker in the installed WSL2 environment; the core application does not require it
Wicker superfamily call: yes — Wicker et al. 2007 class and superfamily from structural and domain evidence (app/backend/teagle_core/classify.py)
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: yes — withholds the superfamily where translation order is unreadable across strands, states when the domain scan did not run, and reports how many reading frames were left unsearched (app/backend/teagle_core/classify.py)
Per-call confidence reported: yes — a confidence level and a separate domain completeness, reported as two independent axes
PCR primer design: yes — Primer3 in-process, with QC on each pair
In-silico PCR: yes — predicted amplicons against the supplied template
Whole-genome off-target scan: yes — isPcr against a whole assembly, in the optional WSL2 environment
Machine-readable provenance record: yes — content-addressed manifest carrying application and database versions, checksums, the input hash and 21 sealed parameters, 17 of them detector thresholds read from the signatures of the functions that apply them and the remaining 4 module-level constants (app/backend/engine.py::_detector_parameters)

Version: 4.2.4 (released 2026-06-05, per repeatmasker.org news announcement; adds FamDB support for Dfam 4.0)
Primary reference: No primary peer-reviewed journal article. Conventionally cited as: Smit AFA, Hubley R, Green P. RepeatMasker Open-4.0. 2013-2015. http://www.repeatmasker.org (no DOI). Do not substitute Tarailo-Graovac & Chen 2009 Curr Protoc Bioinformatics — that is a protocol paper about using RepeatMasker, not the tool's own reference.
Input granularity: both — accepts any FASTA file, single sequence or multi-sequence/whole genome (animalgenome.org manual; repeatmasker.org). It is a library-based screening tool, not a discovery tool, at any scale.
De novo structural detection: no — identifies repeats purely by alignment (cross_match) to a reference library; the manual states it does not perform structural motif recognition for TSD/LTR/TIR (animalgenome.org RepeatMasker Documentation).
Protein-domain classification: partial — an optional companion mode, Protein-based RepeatMasking (RepeatProteinMask, offered as its own web service at repeatmasker.org/cgi-bin/RepeatProteinMaskRequest), does a translated search against RepeatMasker's TE protein database; this is a supplementary sequence-similarity signal, not an HMM/Pfam-style domain-architecture classifier.
Homology-based family naming: yes — assigns hierarchical Class/Family labels (e.g. LINE/L1, DNA/hAT-Ac) drawn from RepBase/Dfam libraries (animalgenome.org manual; Dfam.org).
Wicker superfamily call: partial — output uses the RepeatMasker/Repbase Class/Family hierarchy. Dfam's own documentation states classifications are cross-linked to the corresponding Wicker et al. (2007) terms where available, but RepeatMasker's native output labels are not themselves framed as 'Wicker superfamily' calls.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — sequence with no library hit is simply left unannotated/unmasked; no documented behaviour of withholding a call below a stated evidence threshold.
Per-call confidence reported: partial — the .out file reports a per-hit Smith-Waterman score and %divergence/%deletions/%insertions relative to the consensus (animalgenome.org manual). This is an alignment-quality statistic, not a calibrated confidence or completeness measure.
PCR primer design: not applicable — out of scope. The tool's own documentation only notes that regions it leaves unmasked are more suitable for primer design done elsewhere (webrepeatmaskerhelp.html); it has no design module.
In-silico PCR: not applicable — out of scope, no PCR simulation feature.
Whole-genome off-target scan: not applicable — out of scope, no primer-screening feature.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — no machine-readable bundle of tool/library versions, checksums and parameters. Library version and RepeatMasker version appear as header text in the .out/.tbl files only, not as a structured record.
Usable without a command line: partial — the distributed package is command-line only, but repeatmasker.org hosts a live official web submission service (confirmed on the current homepage: /cgi-bin/WEBRepeatMasker, plus /cgi-bin/RepeatProteinMaskRequest and /cgi-bin/AnnotationRequest, with a job-queue status page) that lets a user submit sequence and get results through a browser with no CLI.
Runs offline: yes — runs locally against an installed/downloaded library once set up; -lib allows fully custom offline libraries.
Export formats: native .out (annotation table), .tbl (summary), .align, .cat (raw cross_match); optional -gff produces a GFF-style file that historically follows GFF2 conventions — full GFF3 requires the bundled rmOutToGFF3.pl converter (repeatmasker.org/utils/rmOutToGFF3.pl); softmasked FASTA (.masked). No native BED export.
License: Open Software License v2.1 (OSL-2.1) — confirmed from the LICENSE file text in the rmhubley/RepeatMasker (Dfam-consortium) GitHub repository.
Platform: Unix/Linux and macOS (requires Perl 5.8+); no native Windows build. Web server is platform-independent (browser-based).
What it does better than TEagle: TEagle analyses one supplied element; RepeatMasker screens sequence of any size, including full chromosome-scale assemblies, against the deepest available curated repeat-library ecosystem (Dfam/Repbase) in a single pass — a scale and library breadth a single-locus tool cannot approach. It is the de facto field-standard annotator that most downstream pipelines (including RepeatModeler2, EDTA and Earl Grey) call internally.
Sources: https://www.repeatmasker.org/ ; https://www.repeatmasker.org/webrepeatmaskerhelp.html ; https://www.animalgenome.org/bioinfo/resources/manuals/RepeatMasker.html ; https://github.com/rmhubley/RepeatMasker (LICENSE, via GitHub API) ; https://www.repeatmasker.org/utils/rmOutToGFF3.pl ; https://www.dfam.org/classification/tree

Version: 2.0.9 (released 2026-06-11, per GitHub releases; adds support for RepeatMasker 4.2.4 and Dfam 4.0)
Primary reference: Flynn JM, Hubley R, Goubert C, Rosen J, Clark AG, Feschotte C, Smit AF. RepeatModeler2 for automated genomic discovery of transposable element families. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 2020;117(17):9451-9457. doi:10.1073/pnas.1921046117
Input granularity: whole genome — documentation explicitly states 'RepeatModeler is designed to run on assemblies rather than genome reads'; not intended for single-locus/single-sequence input.
De novo structural detection: partial — the bundled LTR structural pipeline (LtrHarvest / LTR_retriever, integrated as the 'LTR structural pipeline' described in Flynn et al. 2020) detects LTR and TSD structural signatures for LTR retrotransposons specifically. There is no equivalent structural module for TIR elements. This capability is attributable to the underlying LtrHarvest/LTR_retriever methods bundled into RepeatModeler2, not a bespoke RepeatModeler2 algorithm.
Protein-domain classification: partial — RepeatClassifier compares candidate consensus families to the RepeatMasker Repeat Protein Database (a translated protein search) as one input signal alongside nucleotide-library comparison; this is not a Pfam/HMM domain-architecture classifier in the InterPro sense.
Homology-based family naming: yes — RepeatClassifier assigns RepeatMasker/Dfam Class/Family labels when its score/overlap filters agree (Flynn et al. 2020).
Wicker superfamily call: partial — same RepeatMasker/Dfam Class/Family nomenclature as RepeatMasker; not framed by the tool itself as an explicit Wicker 2007 superfamily call.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — this is a documented residual bucket, not evidence-threshold abstention. Flynn et al. 2020 state families are labelled 'Unknown' when RepeatClassifier's score/overlap filters fail to reach concordance; this is a fallback label for classification failure, not a stated policy of withholding a call below a defined confidence threshold.
Per-call confidence reported: no — RepeatClassifier applies internal score and overlap filters to select 'high-confidence' matches before labelling, but this filtering is not exposed to the user as a per-call confidence value in the output.
PCR primer design: not applicable — out of scope. RepeatModeler2 builds a de novo repeat family library; it has no primer design functionality.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — Stockholm-format seed alignments 'preserve the provenance of the family's representative sequences' (Flynn et al. 2020), but there is no machine-readable, run-level bundle of tool/database versions, checksums and parameters.
Usable without a command line: no — command-line only; no GUI documented.
Runs offline: yes — runs locally on installed genome/library data; the underlying RMBlast search engine reports anonymous usage statistics by default, which can be disabled via an environment variable (per repository docs), but this does not require network access to function.
Export formats: FASTA consensus library, Dfam-compatible Stockholm seed alignments, and a text run log. It does not itself produce genome annotations (no native GFF3/BED) — its library output must be piped into RepeatMasker for genome-wide annotation.
License: Open Software License v2.1 (OSL-2.1) — confirmed from LICENSE file text in the Dfam-consortium/RepeatModeler GitHub repository.
What it does better than TEagle: TEagle characterizes one supplied element and does not discover new families. RepeatModeler2 automates de novo discovery of previously uncatalogued repeat families across an entire genome assembly, integrating multiple structural- and homology-based discovery algorithms (RECON, RepeatScout, LTR pipeline) with automated classification — a genome-scale novel-family-discovery task outside TEagle's single-locus scope.

Primary reference: Ou S, Su W, Liao Y, Chougule K, Agda JRA, Hellinga AJ, Lugo CSB, Elliott TA, Ware D, Peterson T, Jiang N, Hirsch CN, Hufford MB. Benchmarking transposable element annotation methods for creation of a streamlined, comprehensive pipeline. Genome Biol. 2019;20:275. doi:10.1186/s13059-019-1905-y (Author Correction 2022: doi:10.1186/s13059-022-02645-7)
Input granularity: whole genome — described in its own README as an 'automated whole-genome de-novo TE annotation' pipeline.
De novo structural detection: yes, with attribution — LTR structure and TSDs are detected via the bundled LTRharvest/LTR_FINDER/LTR_retriever chain (structural/TSD validation logic documented primarily in Ou & Jiang 2018, Plant Physiol, for LTR_retriever, rather than spelled out independently in EDTA's own README); TIR structure via bundled TIR-Learner; Helitrons via bundled HelitronScanner. These are EDTA's own pipeline components, but the structural-detection methodology itself is described in those components' own publications.
Protein-domain classification: partial — LTR retrotransposon candidates are additionally screened/classified via the bundled TEsorter tool against the REXdb protein-domain database (HMMscan-based detection of capsid, protease, RT, RNase H, integrase domains). This applies to the LTR module only; TIR/Helitron modules use structural and nucleotide-homology methods, not protein domains.
Homology-based family naming: yes — integrates RepeatMasker/RepeatModeler searches against Dfam/RepBase-derived and user-curated libraries to name families.
Wicker superfamily call: yes — EDTA's own documentation states TEs are classified 'into the superfamily level and using the three-letter naming system reported in Wicker et al. (2007)'.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — this is a documented residual bucket, not evidence-threshold abstention. Sequences that pass structural filters but fail homology/domain classification are output tagged 'unknown'/unclassified; this is a fallback category rather than a stated policy of withholding a call below a defined confidence threshold.
Per-call confidence reported: partial — distinguishes structurally 'intact' vs. fragmented TE calls and reports LTR sequence identity (used for age estimation) per element; this is a structural-completeness/quality signal, not a single unified per-call confidence score.
PCR primer design: not applicable — out of scope, no primer design module.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — produces run logs and summary tables (including annotation-inconsistency/benchmarking metrics via its lib-test.py script: sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, precision, FDR, F1), but no single machine-readable bundle of tool/database versions, checksums and parameters per run.
Usable without a command line: no for core EDTA — command-line only. Note: a separate, independently published third-party wrapper, EDTA-GUI (Costa et al. 2026, BMC Genomics, doi:10.1186/s12864-026-12588-z, built on EDTA v2.2.1), adds a graphical front end; it is not part of core EDTA and carries its own citation.
Runs offline: yes — installed via conda/mamba, Docker, or Singularity; runs offline after setup.
Export formats: FASTA TE consensus library (*.TElib.fa), GFF3 whole-genome annotation covering both structurally intact and fragmented elements (*.TEanno.gff3), a BED-like MAKER-masked coordinate file, and tab-delimited summary tables.
License: GPL-3.0 — confirmed from the LICENSE file in oushujun/EDTA (GitHub API license metadata and raw LICENSE text).
Platform: Linux (conda-preferred), HPC/Singularity, macOS and Apple-silicon via Docker/Rosetta 2.
What it does better than TEagle: TEagle analyses a single supplied element. EDTA integrates structural, homology and protein-domain evidence into one automated pipeline that produces genome-wide, Wicker-superfamily-labelled annotations distinguishing structurally intact from fragmented copies across an entire assembly — a genome-scale integration task outside TEagle's single-locus scope. Its 2019 paper also established the benchmarking framework (curated rice TE library) against which later tools, including Earl Grey, are compared.
Sources: https://github.com/oushujun/EDTA ; https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-019-1905-y ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12924346/ (EDTA-GUI) ; GitHub API repos/oushujun/EDTA (tags, releases, LICENSE)

Version: v7.3.0 (released 2026-07-23, per GitHub releases, TobyBaril/EarlGrey). Note the primary paper (2024) describes an earlier release line documented as compatible with Dfam 3.6 onward — capabilities below are cited to the paper unless otherwise noted, and may not all describe v7.3.0 exactly.
Primary reference: Baril T, Galbraith JG, Hayward A. Earl Grey: A Fully Automated User-Friendly Transposable Element Annotation and Analysis Pipeline. Mol Biol Evol. 2024;41(4):msae068. doi:10.1093/molbev/msae068
Input granularity: whole genome — a genome-assembly annotation pipeline.
De novo structural detection: yes, with attribution — de novo family discovery via bundled RepeatModeler2, with LTR structural/TSD signatures detected via bundled LTR_Finder (v1.07) run in parallel; this structural-detection capability is provided by the bundled third-party components per the paper's Methods, not a bespoke Earl Grey algorithm. No explicit TIR-structure detection module is documented.
Protein-domain classification: not documented — no mention in the paper or repository of an HMM/Pfam/REXdb protein-domain classification step.
Homology-based family naming: yes — classification via RepeatMasker searched against Dfam and/or RepBase libraries.
Wicker superfamily call: partial — Earl Grey applies the Wicker et al. (2007) 80-80-80 rule (as implemented by Goubert et al. 2022) during clustering to delineate TE family boundaries; final class/family labels still come from RepeatMasker/Dfam/RepBase nomenclature rather than an explicit 'superfamily' output field.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — this is a documented residual bucket, not evidence-threshold abstention. Elements without a database match are tagged 'unclassified' in the output; this is a fallback label rather than a stated policy of withholding a call below a defined evidence threshold.
Per-call confidence reported: partial — reports per-annotation sequence divergence (used to build repeat-landscape plots) and consensus length/boundary accuracy from its iterative BLAST-Extract-Align-Trim (BEAT) curation step; not a single unified per-call confidence score.
PCR primer design: not applicable — out of scope, no primer design module.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — summary tables/logs record run-level parameters and outputs, but no single machine-readable bundle of tool/database versions, checksums and parameters is documented.
Usable without a command line: no — command-line tool; also distributed via Docker, Singularity and a Gitpod cloud environment, but all remain command-driven, not GUI.
Runs offline: partial — the README states users 'MUST download the required Dfam partitions before running analyses' via a configure_dfam40.sh helper script, so initial setup requires network access; runs offline thereafter.
Export formats: GFF3 and BED annotation coordinates, FASTA (strained TE library, combined library, soft-masked genome), summary PDFs/plots (pie charts, repeat-landscape/divergence plots), tab-delimited and markdown-formatted summary tables.
License: Open Software License v2.1 (OSL-2.1) — confirmed from LICENSE file text in TobyBaril/EarlGrey GitHub repository.
Platform: Linux (Ubuntu) via conda, Docker, or Singularity; Gitpod for browser-based cloud access (still CLI within that environment).
What it does better than TEagle: TEagle analyses one supplied element. Earl Grey automates the full discovery-to-curation pipeline genome-wide, including iterative consensus boundary refinement (BEAT), and is validated on a purpose-built benchmark of nine simulated genomes (250/400/800 Mb; 21/42/58% GC) with 11,883 inserted TE sequences from 30 Dfam v3.7 families, scored by Matthews Correlation Coefficient: Earl Grey averaged MCC 0.97 vs. RepeatModeler2 0.94 vs. EDTA 0.67, plus additional validation on a real Drosophila melanogaster genome (release 6.52) assessing consensus length, coverage and annotation fragmentation. This genome-scale, ground-truth-benchmarked validation is a different exercise from TEagle's single-locus scope.
Sources: https://academic.oup.com/mbe/article/41/4/msae068/7635926 (doi:10.1093/molbev/msae068) ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11003543/ (full text, benchmarking numbers) ; https://github.com/TobyBaril/EarlGrey ; GitHub API repos/TobyBaril/EarlGrey (tags, releases, LICENSE)

Primary reference: Zhang R-G, Li G-Y, Wang X-L, Dainat J, Wang Z-X, Ou S, Ma Y. TEsorter: an accurate and fast method to classify LTR-retrotransposons in plant genomes. Horticulture Research 2022;9:uhac017. doi:10.1093/hr/uhac017
Input granularity: both - ELEMENT mode (default) takes individual pre-identified TE/LTR sequences; GENOME mode (added v1.4) scans whole-genome FASTA for TE protein domains
De novo structural detection: no - does not detect LTR/TIR/TSD from sequence; it classifies sequences that are already identified as TEs (typically by LTR_retriever or a de novo repeat finder upstream)
Protein-domain classification: yes - hmmscan of translated ORFs against REXdb (default; Viridiplantae v4.0 / Metazoa v3.1), plus optional GyDB, SINE and LINE/RT domain databases
Homology-based family naming: no - does not query Dfam/RepBase for naming; classification is via REXdb/GyDB profile-domain hits, not whole-sequence homology to a curated library
Wicker superfamily call: yes - cls.tsv output reports Order and Superfamily columns following Wicker-style nomenclature, plus a REXdb Clade (lineage) column below superfamily level
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no - fallback bucket, not documented abstention. README: 'Many LTR-RTs cannot be classified due to no hit' (incomplete database, mutation/domain loss, or false-positive input); such sequences are recorded as un-classified with Domains='none'. This is the inverse of abstention: unclassified elements are, by default, re-attempted in a 'pass-2' BLAST-similarity step against already-classified elements unless disabled with a flag.
Per-call confidence reported: partial - no single per-call confidence score; reports per-domain E-value/coverage in the domain table and a binary Complete (yes/no) status per element, plus paper-level clade-assignment success rates (76.8-91.9% of Copia/Gypsy elements assigned to clade)
PCR primer design: not applicable - classification tool only, no wet-lab primer functionality by design
Machine-readable provenance record: partial - output filenames/headers encode which reference database and version were used (e.g. '.rexdb.'), but there is no single machine-readable manifest bundling tool version, database checksum, and full parameter set per run
Runs offline: yes - reference HMM databases ship/install locally, no network call needed at runtime
Export formats: GFF3 (domain annotations), FASTA (domain protein sequences, masked/unmasked TE sequences), TSV (cls.tsv classification table), RepeatMasker-format library
License: GPL-3.0 (LICENSE file, GNU GPL v3, 29 June 2007)
What it does better than TEagle: Resolves classification below the superfamily level to REXdb lineage/clade (e.g. specific Copia/Gypsy clades), which most sequence-only classifiers do not attempt; supports multiple domain databases (REXdb, GyDB, SINE, LINE); GENOME mode (v1.4+) lets it scan whole assemblies directly rather than requiring pre-cut single-element input, which TEagle's stated single-locus scope does not cover.

Version: Paper-cited: DANTE v0.1.9, DANTE_LTR v0.3.5 (Novák et al. 2024). A later DANTE_LTR GitHub README (fetched via a single unverified summarization pass, not corroborated) showed a higher version string; not used here since it could not be independently confirmed - treat GitHub HEAD version as not documented for this table.
Primary reference: Novák P, Hoštáková N, Neumann P, Macas J. DANTE and DANTE_LTR: lineage-centric annotation pipelines for long terminal repeat retrotransposons in plant genomes. NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2024;6(3):lqae113. doi:10.1093/nargab/lqae113 (REXdb domain database itself: Neumann P et al. Mobile DNA 2019;10:1)
Input granularity: both, but split by component. DANTE (domain-finding step): 'FASTA-formatted nucleotide sequences, ranging from a few hundred nucleotides up to whole genome assemblies' (single sequence or whole genome). DANTE_LTR (structural step): requires a whole genome/contig assembly plus DANTE's GFF3 domain output as input - not designed to run on an isolated single-element sequence.
De novo structural detection: partial, split by component - DANTE itself: no (domain-only annotator, no structural search). DANTE_LTR: yes - detects 5'/3' LTRs (via direct-repeat search of flanking regions), TSD (typically 5 bp direct repeat at the insertion site), and PBS (primer binding site) from sequence, downstream of DANTE's domain calls.
Protein-domain classification: yes - similarity search (LASTAL, not HMM profiles) of translated frames against the REXdb protein-domain database; qualifier: axis asks for domain-architecture classification generally, DANTE satisfies it via alignment-based domain search rather than HMMER profile search
Homology-based family naming: yes - each domain hit is assigned to a named REXdb lineage entry (e.g. Class_I|LTR|Ty3/gypsy|...), reported as Best_Hit/classification attributes in GFF3; this is a curated reference-library homology call, functionally analogous to Dfam/RepBase naming but against REXdb specifically, not Dfam/RepBase itself
Wicker superfamily call: yes - paper explicitly invokes Wicker et al. 2007 terminology: 'Autonomous plant LTR-RTs are divided into two superfamilies, Ty1/copia and Ty3/gypsy', cited to Wicker 2007
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: partial - documented graded retreat, not a hard refusal and not a bare 'Unknown' bucket either. Paper: 'If the top hits contain sequences from multiple lineages, the next highest classification level (formally, the lowest common ancestor)... is reported' rather than forcing a single (possibly wrong) lineage call. DANTE_LTR additionally supports a '--fallback_mode {none,coarse3,coarse2}' option that demotes ambiguous calls to a coarser rank while preserving the discarded finer call as Original_Classification, and uses a rank system (from full DLTP down to domains-only D) that leaves incompletely-evidenced elements at a lower rank rather than asserting completeness. This withholds specificity rather than fabricating it, which is closer to abstention than a simple fallback label, but it is not a documented full non-call.
Per-call confidence reported: yes - DANTE reports per-domain Identity %, Similarity score, Relative Length, Relative Interruptions and DB-length coverage proportion; DANTE_LTR's DLTP/DLP/DLT/DL/D rank is a documented per-call completeness measure
PCR primer design: not applicable - annotation tool only, no wet-lab primer design by design (note: DANTE_LTR detects an in-silico PBS motif as a structural feature, which is not the same as PCR primer design)
Machine-readable provenance record: partial - GFF3 output retains database hit identifiers, alignment scores, and (for DANTE_LTR) Original_Classification when a fallback demotion is applied, but this was not independently confirmed against the live repository beyond the paper's description; no single machine-readable manifest of tool+database versions/checksums per run is documented
Usable without a command line: partial - core tools are command-line (conda-installable), but both are also distributed as Galaxy Tool Shed tools, giving a browser-based GUI route with no local command line required
Runs offline: yes - REXdb and code install locally; runs without network access once installed
Export formats: GFF3 (primary annotation output), FASTA (extracted domain/element sequences, RepeatMasker-format library via companion script)
License: GPL-3.0 (stated in the paper; DANTE_LTR repository also lists GPL-3.0-only)
Platform: Linux/Unix, conda-installable; also runnable via Galaxy (web) without local install
What it does better than TEagle: DANTE_LTR is benchmarked at whole-genome scale across 93 plant genomes and reported to recover more intact LTR-RTs than several established de novo pipelines - a genome-scale structural+domain integration TEagle's single-locus scope does not attempt. Its graded DLTP-to-D completeness rank and lowest-common-ancestor lineage fallback give a transparent, documented way to report partial evidence rather than a binary classified/unclassified call. Also offers a no-install Galaxy GUI path.

Version: no versioned release tag found on GitHub (repository shows commits, not release numbers) as of the article's submission; article: Biology 2025, 15(1):59, published 29 Dec 2025
Primary reference: Bickmann L, Rodriguez M, Jiang X, Makałowski W. Transformer-Based Classification of Transposable Element Consensus Sequences with TEclass2. Biology (Basel) 2025;15(1):59. doi:10.3390/biology15010059 (preprint: bioRxiv 2023.10.13.562246)
Input granularity: single element/locus only - operates on individual FASTA-formatted TE consensus sequences/models; not designed to scan a whole genome assembly
De novo structural detection: no - classifies pre-existing consensus sequences purely via a transformer model over k-mer tokenization; does not search for LTR/TIR/TSD structural features
Protein-domain classification: no - classification is sequence-pattern-based (k-mer/transformer), not protein-domain/HMM based; no domain search is performed
Homology-based family naming: no - no Dfam/RepBase (or other curated-library) homology search is performed; labels come from the trained classifier's learned categories, not from sequence alignment to a reference library
Wicker superfamily call: partial - the 16 output labels (Copia, Gypsy, hAT, Helitron, TcMar, etc.) are superfamily-level terms, but several (Jockey, L1_L2, RTE, Pao) are RepBase-style clade/family names rather than terms from the Wicker 2007 scheme itself, so the label set only partially maps onto formal Wicker superfamily nomenclature
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no - fallback is not built into default runtime behavior. Per-class softmax scores are reported for every input, and the README states scores above ~0.7 are 'highly accurate' as user guidance for manual interpretation; the classifier always outputs its highest-scoring label by default ('The predicted TE label is the one with the highest score'). The paper's own benchmark manually re-filtered results at a 0.7/0.9 cutoff after the fact (e.g. reducing 667 Drosophila models to 281 at 0.9) to illustrate what stricter thresholding *could* achieve - this is a user-driven post-hoc analysis, not a documented default withholding behavior of the tool.
Per-call confidence reported: yes - reports a per-class softmax probability score for every candidate label per input sequence
PCR primer design: not applicable - classification tool only, no primer/PCR functionality by design
Machine-readable provenance record: not documented - no machine-readable manifest of model version/training-database checksum/parameters found bundled with output
Usable without a command line: yes - hosted web tool (https://bioinformatics.uni-muenster.de/tools/teclass2/index.pl) allows classification and even model training without any command line, in addition to an offline GitHub CLI/Docker route
Runs offline: yes - source and pretrained models are downloadable from GitHub for local/offline use (Conda or Docker), independent of the web tool
Export formats: tab-delimited/TSV table of predicted label plus per-label softmax scores; downloadable via the web tool or written directly by the CLI
License: not documented - the article itself is CC BY 4.0 (open access, per journal policy), but no LICENSE file or badge was found in the IOB-Muenster/TEclass2 GitHub repository governing the source code
Platform: web (browser, any OS) and command-line (Linux, via Conda/Docker) - the only one of the four with a genuine no-install GUI as its primary distribution channel
What it does better than TEagle: The only one of the four with no dependency on a curated reference library (Dfam/RepBase/REXdb) at all - it can attempt a call on elements with no known homolog, which library-dependent tools structurally cannot do. Ships a public, zero-install web interface for both classification and custom model (re)training, which none of the other three offer.

Version: REPET 2.2 standalone package (as distributed at time of PLOS ONE 2014 publication); consulted Aug 2026 - no later PASTEC-specific version number found
Primary reference: Hoede C, Arnoux S, Moisset M, Chaumier T, Inizan O, Jamilloux V, Quesneville H. PASTEC: An Automatic Transposable Element Classification Tool. PLOS ONE 2014;9(5):e91929. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0091929
Input granularity: single element/locus only - classifies TE consensus sequences (typically produced de novo by REPET's TEdenovo pipeline upstream); does not itself take a whole genome as input
De novo structural detection: partial - detects terminal repeats (LTR/TIR, via a custom search: min length 10 bp, min identity 80%, max length 7000 bp) and other structural signals (poly-A tails, ORFs, SSRs via Tandem Repeat Finder) from the sequence alone. Does NOT detect TSD itself: the paper attributes TSD detection (via genome context) to a different tool, REPCLASS, not to PASTEC.
Protein-domain classification: yes - HMMER3 profile search of six-frame translations against TE-specific and non-TE-specific HMM profile databases (distributed from the REPET download directory)
Homology-based family naming: yes - BLASTX/TBLASTX search against RepBase Update for homology-based naming; no explicit Dfam support documented
Wicker superfamily call: yes - the paper states PASTEC classifies to order level for all nine Wicker autonomous orders plus three non-autonomous orders (LARD, TRIM, MITE), explicitly built on the Wicker 2007 hierarchy
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: partial, and the mechanism is real and documented (not merely an Unknown bucket) - a genuine no-match case is labeled 'noCat' (a fallback bucket, comparable to TEsorter's un-classified). But PASTEC also documents a graded retreat when evidence is ambiguous rather than insufficient: 'If PASTEC cannot classify a TE to order level, it classifies it to class level' (withholds order-level specificity), and flags a TE 'potential chimeric' when at least two classifications are equally supported, reporting all candidates pipe-separated rather than forcing one. So both a no-match fallback (noCat) and a documented graded/multi-candidate retreat coexist; PASTEC does not silently pick a single best guess when evidence conflicts.
Per-call confidence reported: yes - explicit per-call 'confidence index' normalized to 100, with a documented additive scoring rule (e.g. +2 for ENV domain presence, +1 per corroborating profile combined with an LTR, +1 per profile found in-frame in the same ORF, +2 per blastx/tblastx hit type, +1/-1 for length plausibility)
PCR primer design: not applicable - classification tool only, no primer/PCR functionality by design
Machine-readable provenance record: not documented - output table records classification, features, and confidence index per element, but no bundled record of database version/checksum or full parameter set was found
Usable without a command line: no - command-line only; standalone or as a REPET module, with parallelized (Sun Grid Engine/Torque) and non-parallelized variants
Runs offline: yes - runs fully offline once HMM/RepBase databases are installed locally
Export formats: tabular text output only (TE name, length, orientation, class, order, completeness status, confidence index, and supporting features); no native GFF3/BED/FASTA/spreadsheet/figure export documented for PASTEC itself (FASTA libraries are handled by the surrounding REPET pipeline, not PASTEC's own output)
License: CeCILL (French free-software copyleft license; strong-copyleft, GPL-compatible) - stated for the REPET package / PASTEClassifier distribution
Platform: Linux/Unix only; parallel variant requires a Sun Grid Engine or Torque cluster
What it does better than TEagle: Broadest Wicker-scheme coverage of the four: explicitly targets all nine Wicker autonomous orders plus three non-autonomous orders (LARD/TRIM/MITE), where the others cover a narrower slice (e.g. TEsorter and DANTE focus on Class I LTR-RTs). Combines structural (terminal-repeat/ORF/poly-A) evidence with HMM-domain and RepBase-homology evidence in one integrated call, and is embedded in the REPET de novo pipeline for full genome-scale library building, which a single-locus classifier does not attempt.

Primary reference: Ou S, Jiang N (2018) LTR_retriever: A Highly Accurate and Sensitive Program for Identification of Long Terminal Repeat Retrotransposons. Plant Physiology 176(2):1410-1422. doi:10.1104/pp.17.01310
Input granularity: both (whole-genome scale in practice, but see denovo_structural qualifier)
De novo structural detection: partial — Module 3 re-derives TSD (default 5 bp, flexible to 3-4 bp) and exact LTR boundary/TG..CA motif from sequence, and Module 1 enforces length limits (100 bp - 15 kb) and a benchmarked 90% minimum LTR-identity floor to control false positives; but LTR_retriever does not scan a raw genome itself — it requires candidate LTR-RT coordinates supplied by an upstream de novo scanner (LTRharvest, LTR_FINDER, or MGEScan-LTR).
Protein-domain classification: yes — Module 5 runs a pHMM search against 102 curated TE-related protein-domain profiles (47 LTR-RT-specific: 30 Gypsy, 9 Copia, 8 unknown) to classify Copia/Gypsy content and filter false positives.
Homology-based family naming: no — classification uses LTR_retriever's own internal curated pHMM protein-domain library, not an alignment/naming step against an external curated nucleotide library such as Dfam or RepBase.
Wicker superfamily call: yes — reports Copia vs Gypsy (the two Wicker 2007 LTR-order superfamilies) from protein-domain content.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — candidates failing identity/length/structural filters are silently dropped from .pass.list rather than flagged with a documented low-confidence/abstain marker; no 'insufficient evidence' output category is documented.
Per-call confidence reported: no per-call score / partial at genome level — the package computes the LTR Assembly Index (LAI), but LAI is a genome-assembly-continuity metric, not a per-element confidence; Ou & Jiang 2018 report only aggregate sensitivity (91.8%)/specificity (94.7%)/precision (90.6%), not a per-call value.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — outputs (.pass.list, .LTRlib.fa, .gff3) are not documented as including a bundled machine-readable record of tool/database versions and parameters.
Usable without a command line: no — 'LTR_retriever is a command line program (in Perl)' (README); no GUI documented.
Runs offline: yes — runs locally, but depends on local installs of TRF, BLAST+, HMMER, RepeatMasker.
Export formats: GFF3 (.pass.list.gff3), FASTA (.LTRlib.fa element and non-redundant libraries), tab-delimited summary lists (.pass.list, family/superfamily size lists). No native BED, spreadsheet, or vector-figure export documented.
Platform: Linux/macOS (POSIX command line); no native Windows build documented
What it does better than TEagle: Filters and classifies LTR-RT candidates across an entire assembly in one run, assembling a non-redundant, genome-specific LTR-RT library ready for RepeatMasker, and computes the LAI genome-assembly-continuity metric — genome-wide library curation and assembly QC a single-locus tool does not attempt.

Version: GenomeTools v1.6.6 (tagged release, 6 Oct 2025); consulted Aug 2026
Primary reference: Ellinghaus D, Kurtz S, Willhoeft U (2008) LTRharvest, an efficient and flexible software for de novo detection of LTR retrotransposons. BMC Bioinformatics 9:18. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-18
Input granularity: whole genome or any multi-FASTA sequence set (operates on an enhanced suffix array index of the target sequence(s)); a single sequence can also be supplied.
De novo structural detection: yes — de novo detection of LTR pairs, from exact-maximal-repeat seeds extended by X-drop alignment, purely from sequence, no reference library needed. Documented defaults (LTRharvest manual, genometools.org/documents/ltrharvest.pdf, rev. 6 Aug 2012): -similar (min. LTR identity) = 85%; -minlenltr/-maxlenltr = 100/1000 bp; -mindistltr/-maxdistltr = 1000/15000 bp; -seed = 30 bp. TSD search (-mintsd/-maxtsd) and start/end motif search (-motif) are OFF by default and must be explicitly enabled by the user; if enabled without an explicit bound, default TSD length range is 4-20 bp.
Protein-domain classification: no — LTRharvest itself performs none; the companion GenomeTools program LTRdigest (also shipped in the gt binary) annotates PBS/PPT and protein domains downstream of LTRharvest predictions, but LTRdigest is a separate tool not requested in this comparison.
Homology-based family naming: no — purely structural detection, no homology search against a curated library.
Wicker superfamily call: not applicable — LTRharvest only flags LTR-RT structural candidates; it makes no superfamily call (that requires LTRdigest or an external classifier).
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — filters are hard thresholds; candidates failing them are dropped silently rather than flagged as low-confidence with a documented rationale.
Per-call confidence reported: partial — reports a per-candidate percentage identity between the two LTR copies (sim(LTRs) column) and structural coordinates, but no composite confidence score.
Machine-readable provenance record: no — with -v/-longoutput, run logs echo the parameters used to stdout, but no structured machine-readable record combining tool version + parameters + database checksums is produced.
Usable without a command line: no — command-line only, invoked as `gt ltrharvest` (part of the gt binary).
Runs offline: yes — fully local C program, no network dependency.
Export formats: GFF3 (-gff3), FASTA of full predicted elements (-out), FASTA of inner regions only (-outinner); default stdout output is a tabular coordinate list. No BED or spreadsheet export documented.
License: ISC license for GenomeTools core (genometools.org/license.html), except a few third-party components under other licenses.
Platform: POSIX systems — Linux, macOS, OpenBSD (genometools.org); no native Windows binary documented.
What it does better than TEagle: Scans an entire chromosome/assembly for LTR-RT candidates in a single suffix-array pass with independently switchable filters for length, distance, identity, TSD and motif — genome-scale de novo discovery a single-locus tool is not designed to do.

Version: binary v1.0.7, as bundled by third-party wrappers (e.g. oushujun/LTR_FINDER_parallel repo path bin/LTR_FINDER.x86_64-1.0.7); the tool's own official release history/date is not documented in sources consulted.
Primary reference: Xu Z, Wang H (2007) LTR_FINDER: an efficient tool for the prediction of full-length LTR retrotransposons. Nucleic Acids Research 35(Web Server issue):W265-W268. doi:10.1093/nar/gkm286
Input granularity: both — single sequence or whole-genome multi-FASTA (original web server capped uploads at 50 MB; compiled binaries remove that cap).
De novo structural detection: yes — detects LTR pairs, target site repeats (TSRs/TSDs) and TG..CA boundary motifs from sequence via exact/approximate repeat search. Minimum LTR similarity (-M), min/max LTR length (-l/-L) and min/max LTR distance (-d/-D) are all user-set at run time; the commonly cited preset -M 0.85 -l 100 -L 7000 -d 1000 -D 15000 is explicitly the LTR_FINDER_parallel wrapper's chosen 'best' parameter set (its README states the wrapper itself sets no defaults), not LTR_FINDER's own compiled-in default, which is not documented in the sources consulted.
Protein-domain classification: yes — searches all six reading frames for reverse-transcriptase (RT) conserved subdomains via dynamic programming, and locates integrase (IN) and RNase H (RH) domains via PS_SCAN/PROSITE patterns.
Homology-based family naming: partial — PBS is predicted by alignment to a species-specific tRNA database, a homology step, but this identifies the tRNA primer only, not a Dfam/RepBase family name for the element.
Wicker superfamily call: not documented — RT/IN/RH domain order differs between Copia and Gypsy and LTR_FINDER detects all three domains, but no consulted source (2007 paper, GitHub README) states that its output explicitly reports a Copia/Gypsy superfamily call.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — documented behavior is the opposite: it 'reports possible LTR retrotransposon models in different confidence levels according to how many signals and domains they hit' (GitHub README), i.e. it reports every candidate hitting >=1 signal with a graded score rather than withholding low-signal calls.
Per-call confidence reported: yes — integer score (0-11) per candidate reflecting the count of structural/domain signals detected.
Usable without a command line: partial — originally a free public web server (tlife.fudan.edu.cn/ltr_finder) described in the 2007 paper; when checked in this session (Aug 2026) the host did not respond (connection refused), so current live GUI availability is not verified. Current usage is predominantly via the standalone command-line binary redistributed through third-party GitHub mirrors/wrappers.
Runs offline: yes — compiled binary runs locally with no network dependency (as packaged in LTR_FINDER_parallel/Bioconda).
Export formats: plain-text tabular full/summary reports; optional graphical schematic diagrams (web server only). No native GFF3/BED/FASTA-library export documented for the standalone binary.
License: not documented in sources consulted (original web tool described as freely accessible; no OSI license file located for the redistributed binaries).
Platform: originally a web server (2007, live status unverified in 2026); widely redistributed as a static Linux x86_64 command-line binary.
What it does better than TEagle: As the first web-server tool for ab initio LTR-RT discovery, historically let a user submit raw sequence and get a full-length prediction with graded confidence and RT/IN/RH domain annotation with no local installation — a no-install screening path a desktop tool does not offer (subject to the live-availability caveat above).

Version: V1.0 (SourceForge release archive HelitronScanner_V1.0.zip; Bioconda packages it as 1.0-0); a secondary blog source referred to '1.1' but no corresponding release artifact was located, so 1.0 is used as authoritative; specific release date not documented in sources consulted.
Primary reference: Xiong W, He L, Lai J, Dooner HK, Du C (2014) HelitronScanner uncovers a large overlooked cache of Helitron transposons in many plant genomes. PNAS 111(28):10263-10268. doi:10.1073/pnas.1410068111
Input granularity: both — built for whole-genome scans (identified 64,654 Helitrons across multiple plant genomes) but runnable on any single FASTA sequence.
De novo structural detection: partial — Helitrons lack terminal inverted repeats and do not create target site duplications, so HelitronScanner does not detect TIR/TSD; instead its two-layered local combinational variable (LCV) algorithm detects the conserved 5' TC and 3' CTRR terminal signals directly from sequence. This is de novo structural detection of a different terminal signature than the LTR/TIR + TSD paradigm.
Protein-domain classification: no — purely a terminus/structure scanner; does not search for the Helitron Rep/Helicase protein domain.
Homology-based family naming: no — no alignment step against Dfam/RepBase for family naming is documented.
Wicker superfamily call: partial — detects only Helitron-type termini and reports candidates as Helitrons; Helitron is itself a Wicker (2007) superfamily, so a positive call is implicitly a Helitron call, but the tool performs no separate superfamily-discrimination step and cannot distinguish Helitron from any other superfamily (it was never designed to).
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — documented behavior is graded confidence, not abstention: LCV scores at the 5' and 3' termini give a 'primary confidence level' and element copy number a 'secondary' one; sub-threshold candidates are excluded by the user-set threshold rather than flagged with a documented 'insufficient evidence' state.
Per-call confidence reported: yes — reports per-terminus LCV scores as a primary confidence measure and element copy number as a secondary confidence measure.
Usable without a command line: no — Java command-line tool (scanHead/scanTail/pairends subcommands via `java -jar`); no GUI documented.
Runs offline: yes — runs locally under a local Java runtime.
Export formats: plain-text coordinate/LCV-score tables; downstream pipeline scripts commonly extract FASTA from these, but native GFF3/BED/FASTA export by HelitronScanner itself is not documented in the primary sources consulted.
What it does better than TEagle: Solves a structural-detection problem terminal-repeat scanners cannot: Helitrons have neither TIRs nor TSDs, so HelitronScanner's LCV approach finds a large, otherwise-overlooked element class across whole plant genomes that LTR/TIR-based tools systematically miss.

Version: 201111 (November 2011 release), distributed via CyVerse/TARGeT and GitHub mirrors (e.g. jburnette/MITE-Hunter, Adamtaranto/MITE_Hunter_2); no subsequent official version is documented — later forks only patch BLAST+ compatibility.
Primary reference: Han Y, Wessler SR (2010) MITE-Hunter: a program for discovering miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements from genomic sequences. Nucleic Acids Research 38(22):e199. doi:10.1093/nar/gkq862
Input granularity: whole genome (designed for genome-scale mining; the paper reports the ~380 Mb rice genome processed in ~44 h) though any FASTA sequence set can be supplied.
De novo structural detection: yes — detects terminal inverted repeats (TIRs) and target site duplications (TSDs) directly from genomic sequence via a structure-based, alignment-driven pipeline. Default parameters per the paper: TIR length 10 bp (<=1 bp mismatch); TSD length 2-10 bp (commonly 'TA', 2 bp).
Protein-domain classification: no — MITEs are non-autonomous and typically non-coding; no protein-domain step is performed.
Homology-based family naming: no — output is grouped into MITE-Hunter's own de novo consensus families intended as an input library for downstream homology tools such as RepeatMasker; it does not itself match candidates to Dfam/RepBase.
Wicker superfamily call: partial — classifies candidates into known Class II non-autonomous superfamily categories (Tc1/Mariner, PIF/Harbinger, hAT, MULE, CACTA) by TIR/TSD signature matching, but the paper notes reliance on subsequent manual curation/verification rather than a fully automated, database-driven call.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: no — reports an aggregate false-positive-rate estimate (~8.3% in rice) for the whole candidate set and provides multiple-sequence alignments for manual review, but does not withhold or flag individual low-confidence candidates with a documented abstention state.
Per-call confidence reported: no — no per-candidate confidence/quality score; only the aggregate false-positive rate is reported.
Usable without a command line: no — 'UNIX program pipeline composed mainly of Perl scripts', command-line only.
Export formats: FASTA consensus-sequence library grouped by family, formatted for direct use as a RepeatMasker library. No native GFF3/BED/spreadsheet/vector-figure export documented.
License: not a formal OSI license; distributed free for download/research use with a request to cite Han & Wessler 2010 (CyVerse/TARGeT download page) — no license file text located.
What it does better than TEagle: Purpose-built to mine an entire genome for the highly divergent, largely non-coding MITE class that homology- and protein-domain-based methods systematically under-detect, producing ready-to-use consensus libraries for genome-wide RepeatMasker annotation — a scale and target class outside a single-locus tool's remit.

Version: v2.6.1 (GitHub release, 26 Jan 2022); note the bundled HTML manual text elsewhere references an older '2.3.7' string, a documentation inconsistency noted here for transparency, not a separate release. Consulted Aug 2026.
Primary reference: Untergasser A, Cutcutache I, Koressaar T, Ye J, Faircloth BC, Remm M, Rozen SG (2012) Primer3—new capabilities and interfaces. Nucleic Acids Research 40(15):e115. doi:10.1093/nar/gks596
Input granularity: single element/locus — designed to design primers against one user-supplied target sequence per call; not a genome scanner.
De novo structural detection: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Protein-domain classification: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Homology-based family naming: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Wicker superfamily call: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: yes — with PRIMER_EXPLAIN_FLAG=1, Primer3 returns PRIMER_LEFT/RIGHT/PAIR_EXPLAIN tags giving per-constraint rejection counts (how many candidates failed on Tm, GC%, self-complementarity, etc.), and reports a PRIMER_ERROR tag when no primer pair satisfies the constraints, rather than silently returning an empty or placeholder result.
Per-call confidence reported: yes — each returned primer pair is ranked by a documented penalty/objective-function value (lower = better); a deterministic quality score, not a probabilistic confidence.
PCR primer design: yes — this is Primer3's core function.
In-silico PCR: no — designs primers and checks internal secondary-structure/mispriming against a user-supplied library or the single input template, but does not itself simulate amplification against a genome/database to predict amplicons.
Whole-genome off-target scan: partial — supports PRIMER_MAX_LIBRARY_MISPRIMING / PRIMER_MAX_TEMPLATE_MISPRIMING checks against a user-supplied mispriming/repeat library or the single input template, but does not itself BLAST-screen a primer pair against a whole external genome assembly/database the way Primer-BLAST does.
Machine-readable provenance record: partial — Boulder-IO output echoes back the input SEQUENCE/parameter tags used for a given run, but does not by default emit a structured record of the Primer3 software version, thermodynamic-table version, or mispriming-library checksum alongside results.
Usable without a command line: partial — the primer3_core binary itself is command-line only; GUI/web front-ends (e.g. Primer3Plus, primer3.ut.ee) are separate third-party interfaces built on the same engine, not bundled with Primer3 itself.
Runs offline: yes — runs entirely locally once installed; no network access required.
Export formats: Boulder-IO text (tag=value pairs); a --format_output flag gives a more human-readable text report. No native GFF3/BED/FASTA/spreadsheet/vector-figure export.
Platform: cross-platform C/C++ command-line source; compiles on Linux, macOS, Windows.
What it does better than TEagle: Not scored against TEagle — documented here specifically because TEagle embeds Primer3 as its primer-design engine, so the paper should state plainly that primer design is Primer3, not a novel algorithm.

Version: continuously-updated web service; no discrete version number is published. Consulted Aug 2026.
Primary reference: Ye J, Coulouris G, Zaretskaya I, Cutcutache I, Rozen S, Madden TL (2012) Primer-BLAST: a tool to design target-specific primers for polymerase chain reaction. BMC Bioinformatics 13:134. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-13-134
Input granularity: single locus for the primer-design input; whole-genome/whole-database scope for the specificity check (BLASTs the candidate pair against a full RefSeq mRNA/genome or nr database).
De novo structural detection: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Protein-domain classification: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Homology-based family naming: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Wicker superfamily call: not applicable — not a TE detection tool.
Withholds a call on insufficient evidenc: not documented — Primer-BLAST reports specificity results (on-target vs. predicted off-target hits) per candidate pair rather than an explicit statement of withheld/abstained calls; no consulted source frames this as abstention.
Per-call confidence reported: partial — combines Primer3's penalty score with an explicit per-pair specificity determination (target-only vs. predicted off-target products), which together serve as a practical confidence signal, though not a single unified numeric confidence value.
PCR primer design: yes — uses Primer3 internally to generate candidate primer pairs.
In-silico PCR: yes — predicts amplicon products including product size by locating primer binding sites via BLAST search followed by Needleman-Wunsch global alignment, covering both forward-reverse and single-primer scenarios.
Whole-genome off-target scan: yes — its defining capability: BLASTs each candidate pair against a chosen genome/transcriptome/database (RefSeq representative genomes, RefSeq mRNA, nr, or a user-selected organism) and flags predicted off-target amplicons, tolerating up to a user-set percentage of primer-target mismatches (up to 35% in sensitive mode).
Machine-readable provenance record: not documented — result pages do not appear to include a structured, downloadable record of the underlying BLAST database build/version alongside primer results, per sources consulted.
Usable without a command line: yes — web-based interface only (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/tools/primer-blast); no standalone command-line distribution.
Runs offline: no — requires NCBI servers/internet access; cannot run offline or against an unpublished/private assembly not hosted at NCBI.
Export formats: web result pages/graphics; downloadable tabular/text primer and specificity reports. No native GFF3/BED export documented.
License: public domain / freely available for all users (NCBI/US government work).
Platform: web only (any OS with a browser); no desktop or command-line client.
What it does better than TEagle: Performs genuine global-alignment amplicon prediction with tunable mismatch tolerance against NCBI's curated, continuously updated RefSeq genome/mRNA and nr databases spanning essentially all sequenced organisms — a breadth of reference coverage a local, single-assembly off-target scan cannot match. Conversely, being web-only and queued, it cannot screen a primer pair against an arbitrary unpublished or private assembly, cannot be scripted into an offline pipeline, and has no local/offline mode — capabilities a local scan (such as TEagle's) retains.
